DecryptionUtils.caesar_decipher:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Decrypts a Caesar-cipher ciphertext by reverse-shifting each alphabetic character by the given shift amount while preserving case and passing non-alphabetic characters through unchanged." caesar_decipher]
    [INPUTS]
        <REF> ciphertext </REF>: string "The encrypted text to be deciphered"
        <REF> shift </REF>: integer "The number of alphabet positions that were used during encryption; may be positive or negative"
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
        <REF> plaintext </REF>: string "The fully deciphered text with all characters processed"
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Initialize plaintext as an empty string RESULT plaintext]
            [COMMAND Iterate over every character char in ciphertext one at a time from left to right RESULT char]
            [COMMAND Within the loop, test whether char is an alphabetic character using isalpha() RESULT is_alpha]
            [COMMAND Within the loop, when char is alphabetic, test whether char is uppercase using isupper() to determine the ASCII base offset RESULT is_upper]
            [COMMAND Within the loop, when char is alphabetic and uppercase, set ascii_offset to 65 RESULT ascii_offset]
            [COMMAND Within the loop, when char is alphabetic and lowercase, set ascii_offset to 97 RESULT ascii_offset]
            [COMMAND Within the loop, when char is alphabetic, compute shifted_char as chr((ord(char) - ascii_offset - shift) % 26 + ascii_offset), subtracting ascii_offset to normalize to 0-25, subtracting shift to reverse the cipher, applying modulo 26 to wrap within the alphabet, and adding ascii_offset back to recover the final ASCII code point RESULT shifted_char]
            [COMMAND Within the loop, when char is alphabetic, append shifted_char to plaintext RESULT plaintext]
            [COMMAND Within the loop, when char is not alphabetic, append char to plaintext unchanged RESULT plaintext]
            [COMMAND After the loop completes, return plaintext RESULT plaintext]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

    [ALTERNATIVE_FLOW: char is not an alphabetic character (isalpha() returns False), covering spaces, digits, and punctuation]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Append the original char directly to plaintext without any shift computation RESULT plaintext]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_ALTERNATIVE_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
DecryptionUtils.vigenere_decipher:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Decrypts a Vigenère-ciphered string by reversing the cyclic key-based Caesar shifts for each alphabetic character while passing non-alphabetic characters through unchanged and preserving the original case of every letter." vigenere_decipher]
    [INPUTS]
        <REF> self </REF>: object "Instance providing the decryption key via self.key, a non-empty string used cyclically during decryption"
        <REF> ciphertext </REF>: string "The encrypted input string whose alphabetic characters will be decrypted; may contain any mix of letters, digits, whitespace, and punctuation"
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
        <REF> decrypted_text </REF>: string "The fully decrypted string with the same length and non-alphabetic structure as the input, with each letter shifted back by the corresponding cyclic key character and original case restored"
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Initialize accumulator variable decrypted_text to an empty string to hold the growing decrypted output RESULT decrypted_text]
            [COMMAND Initialize cursor variable key_index to integer 0 to track the current position within the key, starting at the first key character RESULT key_index]
            [COMMAND Iterate over each character char in ciphertext one at a time, processing the entire string from start to finish with no early exit RESULT char]
            [COMMAND Within the for loop over ciphertext, test whether char is an alphabetic character using char.isalpha(); if true, execute the decryption path; if false, execute the passthrough path RESULT is_alpha_branch]
            [COMMAND Within the for loop, on the decryption path (char.isalpha() is true), compute shift as the 0-based integer offset of the current key character by evaluating ord(self.key[key_index % len(self.key)].lower()) - ord('a'), where key_index % len(self.key) wraps cyclically through the key so the key repeats indefinitely RESULT shift]
            [COMMAND Within the for loop, on the decryption path, compute decrypted_char as the character obtained by reversing the shift: evaluate chr((ord(char.lower()) - ord('a') - shift) % 26 + ord('a')), where subtracting shift and applying mod 26 correctly wraps through alphabet boundaries in both directions, yielding a lowercase letter RESULT decrypted_char]
            [COMMAND Within the for loop, on the decryption path, append decrypted_char to decrypted_text in its original case: append decrypted_char.upper() if char.isupper() is true, otherwise append the lowercase decrypted_char as-is RESULT decrypted_text]
            [COMMAND Within the for loop, on the decryption path, increment key_index by 1 to advance to the next key character; this increment occurs only for alphabetic characters so non-alphabetic characters do not consume a key position RESULT key_index]
            [COMMAND Within the for loop, on the passthrough path (char.isalpha() is false), append char to decrypted_text unchanged without advancing key_index RESULT decrypted_text]
            [COMMAND After the loop has processed all characters in ciphertext, return decrypted_text as the final decrypted result RESULT return decrypted_text]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
DecryptionUtils.rail_fence_decipher:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Deciphers a rail fence cipher by reconstructing the zigzag grid pattern from the encrypted text and reading characters back in diagonal traversal order to recover the original plaintext." rail_fence_decipher]
    [INPUTS]
        <REF> encrypted_text </REF>: string "The ciphertext string to be deciphered; its length determines the number of columns in the rail fence grid."
        <REF> rails </REF>: integer "The number of rails (rows) used in the rail fence cipher; must be at least 2 for a valid zigzag pattern."
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
        <REF> plain_text </REF>: string "The recovered plaintext string produced by reading the populated rail fence grid in zigzag traversal order."
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Initialize a 2D list 'fence' of dimensions rails × len(encrypted_text), filling every cell with the newline character '\n' as an unvisited sentinel placeholder; set 'direction' to -1, and set both 'row' and 'col' to 0. RESULT fence, direction, row, col]
            [COMMAND Iterate exactly len(encrypted_text) times: at the start of each iteration, if row equals 0 or row equals rails - 1 (inclusive boundary check on both ends), negate 'direction' to reverse the zigzag; then overwrite fence[row][col] with an empty string '' to mark that position as a slot belonging to the zigzag path; increment col by 1; add 'direction' to 'row' to advance the cursor diagonally. RESULT fence]
            [COMMAND Initialize 'index' to 0 as a read cursor into encrypted_text. RESULT index]
            [COMMAND Iterate over each rail i from 0 to rails - 1 (outer loop); for each i, iterate over each column j from 0 to len(encrypted_text) - 1 (inner loop); if fence[i][j] equals '' (the slot marker set in the pattern-marking pass), assign encrypted_text[index] to fence[i][j] and increment index by 1; cells that do not equal '' are skipped with no action. RESULT fence, index]
            [COMMAND Initialize 'plain_text' to an empty string ''; reset 'direction' to -1; reset both 'row' and 'col' to 0. RESULT plain_text, direction, row, col]
            [COMMAND Iterate exactly len(encrypted_text) times: at the start of each iteration, if row equals 0 or row equals rails - 1 (inclusive boundary check on both ends), negate 'direction'; then append fence[row][col] to 'plain_text'; increment col by 1; add 'direction' to 'row'. RESULT plain_text]
            [COMMAND Return plain_text as the deciphered output. RESULT plain_text]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
